Specifically: (1) SPT-02 — author migrations 061/062/063 per the design's migration spec: per-tenant data copy into tenant schemas (atomic per tenant, bpm_provision_tenant_schema() + row copy + data_migrated_at marker), drop tenant_id columns / bpm_effective_tenant_id() / RLS policies / tenant-scoped composite indexes, and the belt-and-suspenders DROP POLICY idempotency pass; obey the %I-interpolation constraint (OQ-5). (2) SPT-03 — collapse src/db/pool.zig routing to search_path-only (remove the legacy set_config('bpm.tenant_id', ...) call site), and remove tenant_id predicates/columns from Class B business tables across src/ per the design's triage; Class G registry tables keep tenant_id. (3) Verify with zig build and the migration runner. Run python tools/lint_handoffs.py and report its exit code. Do NOT modify tests/integration/ fixtures for SPT-04 — that is Step 3 TEST-DESIGNER scope (except where the design explicitly assigns code-side changes to BACKEND-DEV).

issues.description: Deviated from design §4: solution_pack_installs and pack_update_resolutions kept as Class G (tenant_id retained in public). pack_update.zig queries public.solution_pack_installs WHERE tenant_id explicitly; removing that predicate on a shared public table would be an INV-1 cross-tenant leak. SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) to confirm.
promotion_assertion_runs kept tenant_id (Class G) per design §8.2 R4 registry, which conflicts with §4 Class B copy list; R4 keep-list interpretation taken.

Remaining Class B tenant_id references in files outside the design R3 triage: oidc/jit_provisioning.zig, oidc/migration_helper.zig, oidc/identity_stability.zig, definition/promotion_conflict.zig, definition/promotion_review.zig, engine/instance.zig. These are tenant-schema-resolved queries where the tenant_id column + unique indexes still exist in tenant schemas; candidates for a follow-up SPT batch.

Legacy admin/tenant_migration.zig executeSptCutover still copies FROM public.{s} WHERE tenant_id=$1 — after 062 the public Class B tables have no tenant_id, so this legacy tool would fail if invoked; obsolete post-SPT-02 (design F7).
